title: Planted q-ary Multiprobe GL_d(F_q) Rank-Saturation Bridge: Exact k-Probe Acceptance Laws, First-Moment Indistinguishability, and q-Binomial Rank Stratification

theorems.name: Full-Rank Exact k-Probe Acceptance Law and Universal First-Moment Identity
theorems.statement: For a dimension-d planted subspace B = rowspan(M) in F_q^n and k probes U = (u_1, ..., u_k), whenever rank([M u_1, ..., M u_k]) = k <= d, the number of b in B with <b, u_l> in W (|W| = R) is exactly q^(d-k) R^k. Averaging over all U in (F_q^n)^k yields E_U[N_W(U; B)] = 1_{0 in W} + (q^d - 1)(R/q)^k.

theorems.name: Zero-Free First-Moment Indistinguishability on B \ {0}
theorems.statement: For any zero-free window W in F_q \ {0} of size R, the normalized expected k-probe acceptance mass on B is M_k^(zero-free)(q, d, R) = ((q^d - 1)/q^d) * (R/q)^k, identical to that of an unstructured subset of F_q^n \ {0} of size q^d - 1 for every k >= 1.

theorems.name: Exact q-Gaussian Rank Stratification of Projected k-Probe Matrices
theorems.statement: Under uniform probes U in (F_q^n)^k, P(U) = [M u_1, ..., M u_k] in F_q^(d x k) has exact rank r in {0, ..., min(d, k)} with probability P_rank(r | q, d, k) = q^(-d k) * q_binom(d, r)_q * prod_{j=0}^{r-1} (q^k - q^j), summing to 1 across r.
